description.narrative:
The proposed Municipal Services Development Project - Phase 2 (MSDP 2) finances investments in municipal infrastructure and utility services. It focuses on urban transport, but could flexibly respond to other municipal infrastructure. It will provide (i) proceeds to MDF for financing to selected municipalities for repairing and rehabilitating municipal infrastructure and local utility services, and (ii) capacity development for MDF and municipalities through incremental administration and technical assistance programs.
The MSDP 2 follows the Municipal Services Development Project (MSDP 1) approved in August 2008. It targets high-priority urban transport projects in Tbilisi and other municipalities, which were proposed for additional Asian Development Bank (ADB) financing under the MSDP 1. As available financing under the MSDP 1 is largely committed to other priority investments, a new facility is proposed.

description.narrative: Improved municipal infrastructure, service delivery, and better living conditions in urban areas.

Citizens enabled to benefit from project construction: 20,000 households having access to improved municipal services by 2014 Progress/Status: According to the February 2013 PPMS report, about 390,000 people benefited through access to the improved roads. The improved WSS benefited 72,000 people in 4 municipalities through pressurized quality water for 12-24 hours a day. The water quality is tested according to the national standard for drinking water. In addition, 50,000 people in 2 municipalities were benefited through installation of garbage collection cans and collection trucks. Data Source: MDF progress report, MDF project completion report Actual value:

Fluidity and capacity of city road network to reduce travel costs and time to major commercial and service centers improved by 5% on the upgraded arteries by 2014 Progress/Status: Travel time reduced by more than half. The increased bus services benefit local people. Data Source: Municipal Transport statistics or other agencies as appropriate Base year: 2009

Number of kilometers of pavement and road upgraded in the city increased by 1% by 2014 Progress/Status: Municipal roads in a total length of 101.7 km were improved and upgraded in 27 municipalities. This accounts for more than 2% of the urban roads existing in each participating municipality. Source MDF semi annual report. Data Source: MDF progress report, MDF project completion report Base year: 2009
